title: console: ⌘K / full-page search scope silently truncated to the first 8 nav objects
body:
## Symptom

⌘K global search (and the full-page search) can only find records in a **subset of the app's objects**. Searching an existing record code returns "no results", while the same query against `GET /api/v1/search` directly (with that object in `objects`, or with no `objects` param) matches — the backend index is fine; the UI truncates the scope it requests.

## Root cause

`useRecordSearch` slices its candidate pool to `maxObjectsQueried` (default 8). That cap is meant to bound the per-object fanout fallback, but it was applied to the pool itself — so the `objects` whitelist sent to the single-request `/api/v1/search` only ever named the first 8 nav objects. Which sidebar group happens to come first decides which records are findable; in an app with 40+ searchable objects the rest are unsearchable no matter what the user types, and `searchableFields` configured on those views is dead weight.

## Expected

The searchAll path must send the full app whitelist; the parallel-request cap applies only to the per-object fanout fallback.

Found via real-app dogfooding (os-tianshun-ehr platform defect registry PLAT-DEF-023, on 17.0.0-rc.0).
